newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Militant Sunni leader wounded in Lahore bomb blast.
newsitem.headline: Militant Sunni leader wounded in Lahore bomb blast.

text.p: At least two people were killed and 25 wounded, including the chief of a militant Sunni Moslem group, when a bomb exploded outside a court in the Pakistani city of Lahore on Saturday, witnesses said.
They said a bomb, apparently planted on a motorcycle, exploded at about 12.30 p.m. (0730 GMT) as Azam Tariq, leader of the Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) group, arrived at the court.

Witnesses said a photographer and a policeman were killed on the spot. Most of the wounded were journalists, lawyers and SSP supporters who had gathered to throw flowers at their leader before he appeared at the Sessions Court in the city centre.
Tariq is facing charges of involvement in various sectarian killings of Shi'ite Moslems, who form about 15 percent of Pakistan's predominantly Sunni population of over 130 million.
The bomb blast appeared to be the latest attack in a long-running feud between militant Sunnis and Shi'ites that cost more than 40 lives last year in Pakistan.

The secretary of Iran's National Security Council, Hassan Rowhani, urged the Pakistani government on Thursday to mount a "crackdown on terrorist groups in Pakistan and (prevent) the assassination of Shi'ite Moslems".
